note: One canonical specification of the block cutting, checked by both the Python package and the browser. Written by hand rather than generated, so it cannot inherit a bug from either implementation. The ragged cases are the point: a trailing partial block must be kept whole and permuted with the rest.

cases.name: ragged final block of one, moved to the front
ragged final block stays whole and stays last
block size one is a plain permutation
identity order returns the source unchanged
block larger than half, two blocks swapped
